title: Strings Fundamentals

steps.title: A string is text
steps.content: A string is an ordered sequence of characters. In Python, strings are immutable: operations create a new string rather than changing one character in place.
steps.example: word = 'Bounty'; word[0] is 'B'. Indexing starts at 0.
steps.tip: For a string of length n, valid positive indices are 0 through n−1.

steps.title: Index a string
steps.explanation: C=0, O=1, D=2, I=3. The character at index 3 is I.

steps.title: Slice a substring
steps.content: Slicing uses text[start:end]. The start index is included and the end index is excluded. Negative indices count from the end.

steps.title: Predict a slice
steps.explanation: Indices 1,2,3 are Y,T,H. End index 4 is excluded, so YTH.

steps.title: Common string operations
steps.content: Useful operations include lower(), upper(), strip(), split(), join(), replace() and membership with 'in'. Be careful: split() returns a list, not a string.

steps.title: Trace a string slice
steps.content: A slice includes its start index and stops before its end index.
steps.explanation: Index 1 is 'o' and index 2 is 'd'. Index 3 is excluded.

steps.title: Check a palindrome
steps.content: Compare mirrored positions until the middle.
steps.prompt: Arrange the steps to test whether a word is a palindrome.
options: Stop when indices meet or cross
Compare characters at left and right indices
Move left forward and right backward when they match
steps.explanation: Two pointers move inward while characters match.
hints: A mismatch ends the check early.

steps.title: Reverse a greeting token
steps.content: Build a new string from the end toward the start. The browser lab uses JavaScript.
steps.prompt: Complete the code so it prints edoc.
hints: Loop index from word.length - 1 down to 0.
Append word[i] to reversed each time.
for (let i = word.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) reversed += word[i];

steps.title: Catch an off-by-one index
steps.content: A student thinks the last character of a length-5 string is at index 5.
steps.prompt: What is the last valid index of a string with length 5?

feedback_by_option.2: Index 5 is out of range for length 5.
feedback_by_option.3: Index 6 is also out of range.
feedback_by_option.4: 0 is the first index, not the last.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Python strings is true?

questions.explanation: split returns a list of parts.

questions.prompt: Last valid index of a length-5 string?

learning_objectives: Treat a string as an ordered sequence of characters.
Use indexing and slicing safely with inclusive start and exclusive end.
Apply common string operations and know split returns a list.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The last valid index equals the string length.
common_misconceptions.correction: For zero-based indexing, the last valid index is length − 1.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A string can always be modified in place.
common_misconceptions.correction: Python strings are immutable; operations return new strings.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A slice includes the end index.

worked_examples.title: Check a palindrome
worked_examples.explanation: Mirrored comparisons need at most floor(n/2) checks.

company_applications.practice: Test empty, one-character and repeated-character inputs.
Explain O(n) traversal and avoid costly repeated concatenation.
Use frequency maps and two-pointer palindrome checks.
Trace slices carefully under time pressure.

srs_cards.question: What is the last valid index of a string of length n?
Does a Python slice include the end index?
srs_cards.answer: No. Start is inclusive and end is exclusive.

srs_cards.question: How do you check a palindrome efficiently?
srs_cards.answer: Compare characters from both ends until the indices meet.

quest.story: Service-company coding rounds love index and slice traps. Master boundaries before tackling harder string problems.
quest.mission: Index, slice, reverse and validate strings without off-by-one mistakes.
